recipes.name: Shrimp and Asparagus
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 pound medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Add egg noodles and boil until tender yet firm to the bite, 7 to 9 minutes. Drain and keep warm until needed.
At the same time, bring a small saucepan of water to a boil. Add asparagus, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain.

Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add garlic and cook until fragrant and golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Add butter and lemon juice; cook until butter melts, 2 to 3 minutes. Add shrimp and cook, stirring occasionally, for 1 to 2 minutes. Add mushrooms and asparagus; cook until mushrooms have softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add egg noodles to the saucepan and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper and garnish with Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp and Asparagus
raw_recipe.description: Mushrooms, shrimp, and asparagus cooked in a lemony garlic butter are tossed with egg noodles and Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: Made some changes to this recipe to make it easier and healthier--chopped asparagus into bite-size pieces and sauteed in about 2T olive oil with garlic about 5 min. Add 1 stick low fat marg., lemon juice and frozen shrimp. Served over mini ziti and sprinkled with parmesan. Left out mushrooms as my husband doesn't like them. Using my version the meal is considerably lower in fat and you eliminate a step by not steaming asparagus. Taste was very fresh, light and healthy. Will definitely make this again next spring!

I followed another reviewers suggestion and cooked the asp in 2T olive oil with the garlic until al debate. Then I pushed the asp to the outside of the pan, added 1stick butter, lemon, s&p and the mushrooms. Once that was par-cooked, I pushed mushrooms to outside of pan and added shrimp. Finally I added the cooked pasta and a little more butter. The mushrooms added quite a bit of liquid. This was an easy way to make this a one pan dish. Rave reviews from the whole family. The asp have the dish depth I what would otherwise be a plain dish. It's a keeper -thanks for sharing!

This was delicious. I used gemelli pasta instead of egg noodles, only 1/2 cup butter and less olive oil. Just personal preference for less butter and oil but all the ingredients were perfect together. I thought the gemelli pasta went well with this recipe since it seemed to hold the buttery sauce in the spirals of the pasta. I also followed other suggestions and cooked the asparagus in a large frying pan with some olive oil for 5 minutes adding the garlic during the last minute. Removed the asparagus from the pan, set aside then cooked the mushrooms in the butter for about 5 minutes. Added the shrimp and cooked until just pink. Then added the lemon juice, parm cheese, salt, pepper and asparagus. Once the pasta was cooked combined all together. Will definitely make this again and add to our regular rotation.

Good! Normally I don't make changes then rate a recipe, but I had to lessen the butter--so I did 3/4 instead and added 1/4 white wine. Plus squeezed 1/2 lemon into it. This was super yummy! And the veggies/sauce can all be in one pan! When you get to the butter step, just add the cut up asparagus in too, it only takes a few min to cook. Then add mushrooms, then do the shrimp last--it cooks so fast and gets hard if overcooked! This recipe is fast if everything get prepped ahead! Hubby and I loved it.

I made several changes to make preparation easier and better. I chopped the asparagus first then cooked it. Afterwards I thought maybe adding the raw asparagus to the cooking pasta for the last few minutes might work just as well and save another pot cleanup. I knew the shrimp would be overcooked if I followed the recipe as written, and I only added them after the mushrooms were sauteed. I used only enough olive oil to cover the bottom of my pan, and half as much butter. As I was sauteeing the mushrooms I felt as if the mixture was telling me to add some white wine, so I did. I used penne instead of noodles. The end result was a really delicious dish. It makes a LOT and I'm looking forward to leftovers tomorrow.

Made this delicious shrimp, asparagus and mushroom pasta. The only thing I did differently was to have the shrimp shelled and deveined, asparagus rinsed and snapped into about 1 1/2 inch pieces and mushrooms cleaned and sliced, all done ahead of time. Then after cooking the garlic in olive oil and butter I threw in the shrimp, asparagus and mushrooms and cooked then all together. The cooked pasta was then added and stirred for a few minutes to warm it all up. Lastly, the Parmesan cheese was sprinkled over all and stirred till mixed well. Added a couple splashs more of lemon juice. Done and served with garlic bread! Yum! Great dinner! Thanks. Co Karen

This recipe is delicious and has all of the right ingredients but, like other reviewers, I suggest cooking it differently. Begin by sautéing the garlic in olive oil for a minute or two over medium high heat for n a large skillet. Next, add one stick of butter - a half cup; not a whole cup. Next add the lemon juice, asparagus cut in two-inch pieces and the sliced mushrooms. I used half baby Bella’s and half white ones. Add salt, pepper and crushed red pepper and stir frequently until the asparagus is tender and the mushrooms are reduced. Lastly, add the shrimp and continue stirring occasionally until the shrimp are pink. Serve over noodles, pasta or rice. Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese on top.

In an effort to save on clean up I cooked everything, except the noodles, in one pan; asparagus and garlic first, then mushrooms and shrimp. It came out really good, though I think next time I'll saute the mushrooms before adding. I used way less oil than called for and I did add extra lemon juice because I couldn't really taste it otherwise. Overall, very good.

Wow! This was amazing and so easy. I second the review about just putting the asparagus in with the olive oil and garlic. Then I added the butter and lots of lemon juice and raw shrimp. I added tajin and paprika. Put mushrooms in last. I didn’t make pasta but soaked up the delicious sauce with some sourdough bread. Yum!

Italians don't use cheese in fish or seafood pasta sauces (or at least not in Tuscany, where I lived 8 years). This pasta sauce, if you use olive oil instead of a pound of butter (or at least a combination, heavier on the oil) has the feel of an "olio e aglio" (olive oil and garlic) sauce, which can be made more savory by adding black pepper and pepper flakes. Asparagus and/or mushrooms certainly complement the shrimp, and you can go even further by adding diced fresh tomato and chopped fresh basil or parsley as a finish (uncooked). Nice recipe to build on, but way too buttery for most tastes!

This dish was delicious! My family ate it up despite me doubling the recipe. In addition to salt & pepper, I seasoned this entree well with Slap Ya Mama seasoning that I added to the mushroom & asparagus (after it was steamed) sautéing process in butter and olive oil. I sautéed the shrimp separately in butter and olive oil and used the same seasoning combination. Once the pasta was drained and I combined everything, I sprinkled about 1TBSP of cayenne pepper seasoning in it and it had just enough heat. I invited my neighbors over for dinner the next night (because it yielded so much since I doubled the recipe). My friend doesn’t like spicy foods, but she even ate it and raved about it. It wasn’t “over the top” spicy. It was perfect. BTW: my friend also ate this dish cold and preferred it that way! Go figure! Thank you so much for the recipe. I will make it again!
My husband loved this

I’m giving this 4 stars because I made some adjustments, but otherwise really love this recipe. I only used 3 tablespoons of both the oil and the butter. I added a dash of crushed red pepper flakes to give it a little kick and I used gluten free pasta. Other than those adjustments, I made it as the recipe states and it’s delish!
Awesome dish!

I have made this a couple of times. It is a favorite at our house. My wife loves it. However, the next time I make it I am going to adjust the servings to six, or even four, since it seems like there is too much butter in the recipe.
The butter IS a lot. One stick next time- bc we're making it again
This was good. I followed the advice of others and cooked the veggies together. I did add more seasoning.
Simply delicious and it came together quickly. I followed the recipe and really loved it.
It was delicious

This was delicious. We didn’t have mushrooms so used peppers and sun-dried tomatoes. I think you could use any combination of vegetables but the asparagus is one I’d keep. I did cut the butter by 1/3 and doubled the lemon juice. We enjoyed this so much we made it again the following week! However, with all the butter it probably shouldn’t be enjoyed too often
